title: Fix sparse CSR add aliasing indices between out and inputs
body:
The BLAS bypass for `add(S, S, out=T)` on sparse compressed tensors (`only_sparse_compressed_binary_op_trivial_cases`, from #95293) hands `T` the same crow/col index tensors as `S`, not copies. Any later out-of-place `add(C, D, out=T)` then rewrites `S`'s indices in place. In `test_sparse_add`, `add(S0, S0, out=S1)` and `add(S0, S0, out=S2)` leave all three operands sharing one `crow_indices` buffer. With int32 indices, every later `csrgeam2` call then runs with `csr_row_ptr_C == csr_row_ptr_A == csr_row_ptr_B`. rocSPARSE forbids that overlap, and cuSPARSE doesn't document it as supported. rocSPARSE's `csrgeam_nnz` writes `row_ptr_C[row]` while other wavefronts still read `row_ptr_A[row + 1]`, so under load rows collapse and the test returns wrong values (#167783). With int64 indices the library works on int32 copies, but the result is copied back into the shared buffer, so `S` is corrupted on every backend.

There's a second hazard with in-place `add(E, F, out=E)` or `out=F` when the sparsity pattern grows. `add_out_sparse_compressed_{cpu,cuda}` resizes `out` to `self`'s nnz first. When `out` aliases `other`, that shrinks `other`'s col_indices and values underneath the call. On ROCm this gives wrong values deterministically. On CPU it reads past the shrunk buffers, and with int64 indices it segfaults.

Fix: the trivial-case helper now clones the index tensors before `set_member_tensors`. The add_out paths clone any input that shares storage with `out` (new `sparse_compressed_members_alias` helper). The clone only happens in the aliased case, which includes in-place `add_` on the BLAS path; `x.add_(x)` stays on the trivial path. Making rocSPARSE tolerate the overlap isn't an option (it violates the API contract), and guarding only the CUDA path would leave the CPU segfault.

Adds `test_sparse_add_aliased_out`: `add(A, A, out=B)` then `add(C, D, out=B)`, plus in-place add with a growing pattern for `out=self` and `out=other`, int32 and int64 indices, all devices. Also removes the `skipIfRocm` on `test_sparse_add`; the DISABLED issue #167783 was auto-closed, and the nnz=0 workaround in that test is a separate issue and stays.

Test Plan:

The new test fails 8/8 (cpu and cuda) without the fix, and the unfixed CPU `add(E, F, out=F)` with int64 indices segfaults. With the fix, on gfx950:

```
PYTHONPATH=test python -m pytest test/test_sparse_csr.py -k test_sparse_add_aliased_out
# 8 passed
PYTHONPATH=test python -m pytest test/test_sparse_csr.py -k "test_sparse_add_cuda or test_sparse_add_cpu" --flake-finder --flake-runs=25
# 200 passed, alone and with a GEMM co-tenant plus stress-ng --cpu 64 --vm 4 --vm-bytes 4G (unfixed: 8/750 failed under that load)
PYTHONPATH=test python -m pytest test/test_sparse_csr.py -k "add and not triton"
# 530 passed, 36 skipped
```

This PR was authored with the assistance of an AI agent (Claude). The analysis and test results were verified by hand.
